title: Web Crawler
prompt:
Design a crawler that downloads web pages to feed a search index.

Functional requirements:
- Start from seed URLs, extract links, and keep discovering new pages.
- Respect robots.txt and per-site politeness (no more than one request every few seconds per host by default).
- Avoid storing duplicate content; recrawl pages based on how often they change.
- Store raw HTML for downstream indexing.

Scale:
- Crawl 1B pages per week; average page 100 KB.
- Tens of millions of distinct hosts.

Questions to answer:
1. What does the URL frontier look like, and how does it enforce politeness and priority together?
2. How do you detect already-seen URLs and duplicate content at this scale?
3. How do you distribute the crawl across machines?
4. What traps and failure modes must you guard against?
notes:
ESTIMATES
- 1B pages/week = ~1,650 pages/s; aim for 3-5k/s headroom.
- Bandwidth: 1,650 x 100 KB = ~165 MB/s (~1.3 Gbps).
- Storage: 100 TB/week raw HTML, ~20-30 TB compressed.
- Seen-URL set: tens of billions of URLs over time.

COMPONENTS
- URL frontier, fetchers, DNS resolver cache, robots.txt cache, parser/link extractor, URL normalizer and filter, seen-URL store, content dedup, content store (object storage / HDFS in WARC files), recrawl scheduler.

FRONTIER (Mercator-style)
- Front queues by priority (PageRank-ish score, freshness need, site importance).
- Back queues: one per host, each fetcher thread owns hosts. A heap keyed by "next allowed fetch time" per host enforces the crawl delay.
- Frontier mostly on disk with in-memory buffers at the head and tail of each queue.

DISTRIBUTION
- Partition by hash of hostname to crawler nodes. All URLs for a host land on the same node, so politeness is enforced locally without coordination. Links discovered for other hosts are forwarded to their owning node in batches.
- Consistent hashing to rebalance when nodes join or leave.

DEDUP
- URL normalization (lowercase host, strip fragments, sort query params, remove session IDs).
- Seen URLs: Bloom filter in memory for fast negative checks backed by a persistent KV store (RocksDB) for exact checks.
- Exact content dup: hash of body. Near-dup: SimHash with Hamming distance threshold.

RECRAWL
- Track change frequency per page; schedule next fetch adaptively (frequently changing news pages hourly, static pages monthly). Use conditional GET (ETag / If-Modified-Since).

ROBUSTNESS
- Spider traps: cap URL length and path depth, cap pages per host per crawl, detect repeating path segments, calendar pages.
- Timeouts, max page size, content-type filtering.
- Cache DNS; DNS is a classic bottleneck.
- Checkpoint frontier state so node failures do not lose work.

PITFALLS
- Global politeness via a central lock service; partition by host instead.
- Re-fetching robots.txt per request; cache it per host with a TTL.
- Treating the crawler as BFS only; priority matters for quality.
